With the battle raging on in space, Grievous and his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] kidnapped the Supreme Chancellor, after defeating several Jedi and wounding Council member [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]]. Grievous then transported Palpatine to his flagship, the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]. Several Jedi piloting starfighters attempted to intercept Grievous on his way to the flagship, but they failed. After realizing that they had been lured away from Coruscant, Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi returned from [[Tythe/Legends|Tythe]] to join in the attempt to rescue Palpatine, who was being held aboard Grievous' flagship, the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']].<ref name="LoE" /> Although Dooku injured Kenobi, Skywalker disarmed him, and at the Chancellor's command, the young Jedi Knight ruthlessly beheaded the Dark Lord, and released Palpatine, dealing a tremendous blow to the Confederacy.<ref name="ROTS" />

====Last stand of the Jedi Order====
{{Main|Order 66/Legends}}
{{Quote|In the name of the Galactic Senate of the Republic, you're under arrest, Chancellor.''"<br />"''Are you threatening me, Master Jedi?''"<br />"''The Senate will decide your fate.''"<br />"''I ''am'' the Senate!''"<br />"''Not yet.''"<br />"''It's treason then.|Mace Windu and Palpatine|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
After the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|battle over Coruscant]] concluded, the Jedi learned from Anakin Skywalker that Palpatine was in fact Darth Sidious, the Dark Lord of the Sith, and had been responsible for the war to begin with. [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] led a group of Jedi Masters [[Showdown on Coruscant|to arrest Sidious]], but Sidious managed to kill all four Masters with the help of Anakin Skywalker, who betrayed the Jedi, fell to the dark side and became [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. This was later propagandized by Palpatine as an attempted coup by the Jedi and provided the reason for the start of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] in which most of the Jedi were killed.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:DuelonCoruscant.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Jedi Masters [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], [[Agen Kolar/Legends|Agen Kolar]] and [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]].]]

Just after [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] was issued, [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|forcibly compelling all the clones to kill their Jedi commanders]], Darth Vader went to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] to [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|kill]] the remaining Jedi situated there. Accompanied by the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], Vader killed all of the Jedi, including the younglings, and changed the signal given off by the Temple's emergency [[Jedi beacon/Legends|beacon]] to tell Jedi to return to the Temple. Then, Sidious sent Vader to [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] to [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|wipe out the last of the Confederacy's leaders]], then ordered him to send a deactivation signal to shut down the droid forces, ending the war. Order 66 was successful in wiping out 99% of the entire Order and wiping out the High Council, officially concluding the Order's position as the dominant Force tradition in the galaxy and destroying nearly all of their temples and academies across the galaxy.<ref name="ROTS" />

In a final attempt to save the Republic and the Jedi Order from complete extinction, Jedi Masters Yoda and Obi-Wan Kenobi, two of the most notable survivors of Order 66, embarked on a desperate mission to destroy the Sith. Master Kenobi [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|went to fight Darth Vader]] on Mustafar while Yoda [[Skirmish in the Senate|went after Darth Sidious]] within the bowels of the [[Grand Convocation Chamber|Senate building]] (the latter of whom had just [[Declaration of a New Order|declared himself]] [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]). Vader was defeated, losing much of his organic limbs after suffering grievous lightsaber injuries, necessitating the majority of Vader's body being kept in a [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|mobile life-support system]] to keep him alive. The battle between Yoda and Sidious ended in a stalemate: Yoda was forced to flee with Sidious keeping his life. With Grand Master Yoda and Master Kenobi going into exile, Darth Sidious saw the Sith rise to galactic dominance again.<ref name="ROTS" />

====Great Jedi Purge====
{{Main|Great Jedi Purge/Legends}}
{{Quote|The remaining Jedi will be hunted down and defeated. Any collaborators will suffer the same fate.|Palpatine|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:BeyghorSahdett-Rep79.jpg|thumb|left|140px|Jedi Beyghor Sahdett flees the battlefront after defeating a squad of clone troopers.]]
Despite the fact that many of the most senior Jedi had been betrayed and killed, many Jedi survived Order 66. Sidious, now the Emperor of the galaxy, used Darth Vader and the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]] to hunt down and kill the remaining Jedi. Some Jedi decided to fight the Empire, such as [[Roan Shryne]]<ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> and those at the [[Conclave on Kessel]].<ref name="Purge">[[Purge (comic book)|''Purge'']]</ref> Some hid, like Obi-Wan Kenobi and Grand Master Yoda.<ref name="ROTS" /> Many Jedi fell to Vader,<ref name="Purge" /><ref name="Dark Lord" /> [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitors]],<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]],<ref name="DV:E">{{Tales|issue1=1|issue2=2|Extinction}}</ref> and even [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] who were bent on ending the Order's grip on the galaxy.<ref name="Underworld">{{InsiderCite|89|Underworld: A Galaxy of Scum and Villainy}}</ref> Sidious, in his guise as Palpatine, used the rumors of what had occurred at Master [[Shadday Potkin/Legends|Shadday Potkin's]] failed [[Conclave on Kessel|conclave]] on the planet [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] to cement the image of Vader as a symbol of the Empire to fear, and a further warning to all who stood in his way.<ref name="Purge" /> The official report regarding the events on Kessel prepared by [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] stated that a large group of Jedi had attempted to kill Vader but descended into madness and killed each other in a power struggle while the others were executed for numerous crimes.<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref>

During the Purge, Vader raised a [[Galen Marek|secret apprentice]] in a hope to overthrow Palpatine. In [[3 BBY/Legends|3]]-[[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], the apprentice was sent to find and kill surviving Jedi such as [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]], [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], [[Maris Brood]], and Force-sensitives on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] as a means of training, the only survivor being Rahm Kota.<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] discovered Jedi Master [[The Dark Woman|An'ya Kuro]], also known as the Dark Woman, hiding on the planet [[Cophrigin V]]. Darth Vader arrived on the planet to kill Kuro personally.<ref name="DV:E" /> By this time, the Great Jedi Purge was over, and the Empire would, but still deal with another conflict, the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The most prominent survivors of the Great Jedi Purge were [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]],<ref name="EPV">{{Film|V}}</ref> [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]],<ref name="EPIV" /> [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]],<ref name="Legacy 15">[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]]</ref> [[K'Kruhk]],<ref name="Legacy 11">[[Legacy (2006) 11|''Legacy'' (2006) 11]]</ref> [[T'ra Saa/Legends|T'ra Saa]], [[Qu Rahn/Legends|Qu Rahn]],<ref name="DF2">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> [[Echuu Shen-Jon]],<ref name="Galactic Battlegrounds">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> [[Empatojayos Brand]], and [[Ood Bnar]].<ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]''</ref>

Despite the great loss of life, the former Grand Master had set in motion a plan, a final hope for the Order. Unknown to the Sith, Anakin Skywalker had fathered two extremely powerful children. His son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], was trained in the Force by Master Kenobi and Grand Master Yoda, eventually sending him to defeat the Sith. In a [[Battle of Endor/Legends|climatic battle]], Skywalker defeated his father. Sidious betrayed Vader by ordering Skywalker to kill him and take his place at Sidious's side. When Sjywalker refused, an angry Sidious tortured him with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force Lightning]]. Begging his father to help him brought out the former Anakin Skywalker, who sacrificed his life to destroy Sidious over the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]], bringing an end to Darth Bane's line of Sith. In the decades following the Sith defeat, Skywalker would begin the slow rebuilding process as he gathered together the last remnants of the Order's membership and artifacts. Training a new generation of Jedi, Skywalker's [[New Jedi Order|Order]] materialized, struggling to gain a foothold in a galaxy rife with war and violence.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

==Organization==
===Leadership===
{{Main|Jedi Council/Legends}}
{{Quote|How we conduct war is what distinguishes us from others.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="AWoTF">{{TCW|A War on Two Fronts}}</ref>}}
During the [[Force Wars]], the first Jedi formed a central political entity called the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]].<ref name="SWTOR" /> The High Council was a gathering of great minds that acted as a governing body for the Order, eventually serving as an advisory board for the [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Office of the Supreme Chancellor]] following the Order's joining the Republic.<ref name="TJP" /> The High Council was made up of twelve members at a time, a tradition established as early as the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|organization|thejediorder|Jedi Order, The}}</ref>

Membership on the Jedi High Council was decided by the standing Council and was made up of a series of different terms. Consisting of five lifetime members, four members who stayed on the Council until they chose to step down, and three short term members, who changed regularly and sat on the Council for a relatively short period of time, this method kept the voices and opinions of the Council fresh and focused.<ref name="Databank" /> While membership was usually restricted to [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]], exemptions were sometimes made; allowing a Knight to sit on the Council should certain insight be needed or if they are in the transitional stage before formal elevation. A notable example was Anakin Skywalker, who was appointed by Supreme Chancellor Palpatine in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. While the Council accepted the appointment, they refused to make him a Master.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Jedicouncil2.jpg|thumb|left|260px|The Jedi High Council in 22 BBY.]]
For several generations, the Order was overseen by three additional Councils that oversaw various responsibilities within the Order. The [[Council of First Knowledge/Legends|Council of First Knowledge]] oversaw the [[Jedi academy]] housed within the Coruscant Temple, in addition to direct oversight of satellite training academies and libraries. The members of the Council of First Knowledge were looked upon for advice in situations needing to be contrasted with the past. Jedi on this Council were sometimes former members of the High Council, and could give a different perspective on current events based on past decisions and mistakes.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /><ref name="Darkness">''[[Star Wars: Darkness]]''</ref><ref name="TJP" /> Instead of advising the Supreme Chancellor, the [[Council of Reconciliation/Legends|Council of Reconciliation]] worked closely with the [[Republic Diplomatic Corps/Legends|Republic Diplomatic Corps]] in order to assist in the acquisition of new member worlds in the Senate. Assigning [[Jedi Diplomat]]s and [[Jedi Ambassador|Ambassadors]] to implement treaties and welcome new people into the Republic, the Reconciliation Council's members worked very closely with the Senators on Coruscant.<ref name="CoD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref><ref name="TJP" /> Finally, the [[Council of Reassignment/Legends|Council of Reassignment]] oversaw the [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]] and the placement of individuals who failed the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] or were deemed unfit to continue along the standard path of the Jedi Knights.<ref name="Rising Force">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Rising Force]]''</ref><ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /><ref name="TJP" />

The decisions of these four Councils have shaped the progress of the Republic as well as the Order. When the High Council of the era refused to enter the [[Mandalorian Wars]] and took a more passive stance on the issue until they could assess it, a group of disenchanted Jedi known as the [[Revanchist]]s rose up and incited the [[Jedi Civil War]] nearly wiping out the Order.<ref name="KOTOR" /> When the Order had managed to recover, the Council took a slightly more aggressive stance, culminating in the [[New Sith Wars]] where they actively ruled the Republic as a quasi-military dictatorship. The First Knowledge Council took the time following the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] to purge all references to the Sith from the minds of the galactic populace, ensuring that within a few years of the war, the darksiders' legacy was all but forgotten. A millennia later during the Clone Wars, the twilight years of the Galactic Republic, the Jedi acted as generals, soldiers and military advisers in the conflict before being nearly destroyed once again, by the newly resurgent Sith menace.<ref name="ROTS" />

===Jedi ranks===
{{Main|Jedi/Legends}}
{{Quote|Confer on you, the level of Jedi Knight, the Council does. But agree with your taking this boy as your Padawan learner, I do not!|Yoda to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="TPM" />}}
As the Jedi were instructed in the ways of the Order and of the Force, each member progressed through several different ranks.

[[File:JediTrio-OP.png|thumb|right|220px|L-R: Jedi Master Mace Windu, Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi & Jedi Padawan Anakin Skywalker.]]
*'''''[[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi Initiate]]''''' (or [[Youngling/Legends|''Youngling'']] or "Jedi Hopeful") &ndash; The youngest members of the Order, these [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] children were given the rank of Initiate when they began their communal training in clans. [[Jedi seeker]]s search worlds throughout the galaxy for force sensitive children where blood testing was required upon discovery, Initiates were either in few cases taken from their families or were mostly found orphaned and brought to a Jedi academy for formal training.<ref name="TJP" />
*'''''[[Padawan/Legends|Jedi Padawan]]''''' &ndash; After being selected for individual tutelage under a single Jedi Knight or Jedi Master, Initiates were given the title of Padawan; a word derived from the [[Je'daii Order]]. Eligible for this rank following the successful completion of the [[Initiate Trials/Legends|Initiate Trials]], Padawans were typically taken at adolescence and completed their training away from the academy. Per tradition, Padawans of a hair-growing species would wear a long braid of hair behind their ear; non-haired Padawans were encouraged to wear a type of jewelry, a tattoo, or other body modification. A Jedi Knight or Jedi Master could have only one apprentice at a time. The Padawan had to be promoted to the rank of Jedi Knight before another apprentice could be chosen, a practice that was formalized following the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. While in place, the policy could be revoked should the Order see a decline in number, and necessity forces the apprenticeship of several students to a single master. Following several unsuccessful attempts at the Initiate Trials or if a student is not chosen by a Master, the Council of Reconciliation would place the student within the [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]]. Depending on where the student's talents lay, this might be the [[Agricultural Corps/Legends|Agricultural Corps]], the [[Medical Corps/Legends|Medical Corps]], the [[Educational Corps]] or the [[Exploration Corps/Legends|Exploration Corps]]. If this role did not suit a particular student, they could choose to leave the Order entirely.<ref name="TJP" />
*'''''[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]''''' &ndash; Following a period of nearly a decade of one-on-one training with a master, a disciplined Padawan was eligible to attempt the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]]. Upon successfully completing all tests put forth, a Padawan's braid was severed by the High Council and their life as a Knight began. No longer attached to a master, Knights were free to accept missions from the Council, pursue specialized training on one of the three branches of Knighthood, or take their own Padawan.<ref name="TJP" />
*'''''[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]''''' &ndash; A Knight who showed great understanding of the Force and managed to instruct a Padawan and train them successfully to the level of a Jedi Knight was elevated to the rank of Master by the High Council. Self-declaration of the title was frowned upon and rare practice in the latter days of the Order, but not uncommon during war times or periods of disbandment. Amongst the Order's Masters, only a select few were appointed to one of the Jedi Councils. Made up exclusively of wise, experienced Masters, the Councils of the Order had different levels of membership, ensuring fresh perspectives were expressed as new events occurred. The High Council was made up of 12 masters, five of them holding life terms, four holding long-terms, and three holding short-terms. The elected leader of the Council was known as the [[Master of the Order/Legends|Master of the Order]] and was often bestowed upon the acting [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]]; the recognized leader of the entire Order.<ref name="TJP" />

===Jedi Service Corps===
The [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]] was a group of organizations overseen by the [[Council of Reconciliation/Legends|Council of Reconciliation]] that was maintained as an alternative or a supplement to traditional mission assignments from the High Council. While the majority of the Corps was indeed made up of Initiates who had failed to pass the [[Initiate Trials/Legends|Jedi Initiate Trials]], there were many Padawans, Knights, and Masters whose specializations brought them to the Corps.<ref name="TJP" />

'''Agricultural Corps'''<br />
The [[Agricultural Corps/Legends|Agricultural Corps]] was the largest of these organizations. Members of the AgriCorps would use their [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] to care for crops all over the galaxy, aiding in the feeding of several million citizens of the Republic. Working with the [[Republic Agricultural Administration]], the AgriCorps spread the idea that the Living Force can overcome the horrors of drought and famine. Made up mostly of life-long members that had failed their trials, the AgriCorps had bases on [[Salliche/Legends|Salliche]], [[Taanab/Legends|Taanab]], and [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]].<ref name="TJP" />

'''Medical Corps'''<br />
In the [[Medical Corps/Legends|Medical Corps]], young Jedi learners who were not chosen as Padawans used their healing powers to tend for sick beings in the galaxy. Unlike the AgriCorps, the MedCorps maintained only a few dozen students and their instructors at any given time. Maintaining an infirmary in the [[Halls of Healing]] on Coruscant, MedCorps members worked alongside the [[Galactic City Medical Center]]'s doctors and specialists as they helped treat citizens of the planet-city.<ref name="TJP" />

'''Educational Corps'''<br />
This [[Educational Corps]] consisted of students who were still in training. Overseen by the [[Lore Keeper|Chief Librarian]], the EduCorps members stationed at the Temple on Coruscant cataloged and translated data within the Archives.<ref name="TJP" />

'''Exploration Corps'''<br />
The [[Exploration Corps/Legends|Exploration Corps]] was responsible for exploring the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] as well as the study the history of the Jedi and [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. With refueling centers on nearly every Republic Ordnance or Regional Depots, the galaxy was their territory for exploration. Working closely with the [[Republic Survey Corps/Legends|Republic Survey Corps]] and the [[Intergalactic Zoological Society]], the ExplorCorps had the highest number of Knights and Masters working in its ranks.<ref name="TJP" />

===Jedi sub-sects===
The Jedi Order during its history has often been confronted with schisms regarding the interpretation of the Jedi Code, which sometimes created new thinking minority within the Order. These currents for the most marginalized and ostracized were sometimes tolerated, despite the fear of the return of the Sith and the Dark Side.

'''[[Altisian Jedi]]'''
Founded by the Jedi Master [[Djinn Altis/Legends|Djinn Altis]], the Altisian faction held several precepts frowned upon by the orthodox Jedi Order, including the taking of multiple apprentices by one master, initiating adult Padawans, and allowing families. Leaving the Jedi Temple during the last decades of the Temple, Altis and his followers moved about the galaxy serving as relief workers on underdeveloped worlds and backwaters.

'''[[Corellian Jedi]]'''
Faithful to the reputation of rebels of their people, Corellian Jedi were strongly attached to their natal star system and unwilling to respect the rules of emotional detachment of the Order. So a waiver was granted to them, allowing them to remain in the Corellian system, to raise families and take their own children as Padawans. They soon developed their own cultural identity within the Jedi Order, with traditional green robes, commemorative medals and famous dynasties like the [[Horn family|Halcyon family]].

[[File:IronKnight-NEGD.jpg|thumb|right|130px|A Shard Iron Knight with his lightsaber.]]
'''Paladins'''
Founded by the Jedi Master [[Teepo]] during the [[New Sith Wars]], the [[Teepo Paladins]] and later the [[Gray Paladin]]s acknowledged that a Jedi could be no more independent of the Force than of nourishment or air; nevertheless, they had developed skills and techniques that did not utilize the Force's "flashier" aspects. They didn't eschew the use of lightsabers completely, they simply believed that a Jedi should use which ever weapon he or she felt the most comfortable with, but many chose instead to rely on proficiency with blasters and other forms of combat, both armed, and unarmed. They became Masters in various forms of martial arts like [[Teräs Käsi/Legends|Teräs Käsi]], as well as esoteric weaponry such as [[spinstick]]s, rather than rely on Force-augmented gymnastics and speed. Teepo and his followers were ostracized as potential darksiders. Though not a formal part of the Order, some still maintained residence at the Jedi Temple.

'''[[Iron Knight]]s'''
Founded by the Jedi Master [[Aqinos]], they were Force-sensitive crystalline [[Shard (species)|Shards]] trained as Jedi, who required droid bodies as their hosts to interact with the world. The Jedi Council, however, was horrified that Aqinos had taught inorganic crystals about the Force, and felt that they could not truly understand the Force. Aqinos was excommunicated, and the Iron Knights went with him.

'''[[Potentium]]'''
Founded by the Jedi Master [[Leor Hal]], the Potentium claimed that there was no inherent evil in viewing the Force. They claimed that what others called the light side was actually just the Force itself, which is inherently good. What others therefore called the dark side was a perversion of the Force, twisted by those who used it. Believers of Potentium said that the potential for light and dark sides resided in the user, not the Force itself. And since there was no dark side, there were no dark side actions or Force techniques; in effect any action, good or evil, could be performed without risk as long as the intent was not evil. The followers of Potentium were expelled from the Jedi Order and some of the outcast followers colonized [[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]]. 

===Funding===
During the modern era of the Galactic Republic, the Jedi Order received its funding from the Republic Senate. In exchange, the Jedi offered their services to the Supreme Chancellor and other Republic institutions. This financial support covered the needs of the Order, including the maintenance of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, operational staff, basic provisions for the Jedi themselves, and a modest fleet of vehicles and starships reserved for their use, along with other incidental expenses.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

Jedi assigned to missions were provided with funds tailored to the expected scope of their assignment. While the Temple handled its resources with care, it was not overly restrictive. A Jedi Knight might receive a reasonable amount of credits deemed sufficient for the mission. Padawans, however, were not entrusted with funds directly; any necessities they required were managed by their Masters, who distributed resources as needed.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

Because the Order emphasized modesty and discipline, Jedi were expected to limit their expenses—favoring public transportation, simple meals, and minimal lodgings. On Republic-aligned worlds, Jedi could often rely on cooperation from local authorities. However, when operating covertly or in regions beyond Republic jurisdiction, they were often required to adapt and rely on improvisation.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

Any unused funds, along with any credits obtained during a mission, were expected to be returned to the Temple. In many cases, Jedi found that they required little financial support while in the field, trusting instead that the Force would provide what was truly necessary.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

==Jedi Code==
{{Main|Jedi Code/Legends}}
{{Quote|If you would just follow the Code, you would ''be'' on the Council.|Obi-Wan Kenobi to Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="TPM" />}}
Members of the Jedi Order, from Jedi Masters to Padawans, were encouraged to follow a set of guidelines, including self-discipline, responsibility, and public service. These principles were put simply yet effectively in the Jedi Code:<ref name="Episode I Scrapbook">''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Scrapbook]]''</ref>
{{Quote|''Jedi are the guardians of peace in the galaxy.''
:''Jedi use their powers to defend and protect, never to attack others.''
:''Jedi respect all life, in any form.''
:''Jedi serve others rather than ruling over them, for the good of the galaxy.''
:''Jedi seek to improve themselves through knowledge and training.''|The [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]]|<ref name="Episode I Scrapbook" />}}
Derived from the [[Je'daii Code|Code]] of the [[Je'daii Order]] Master [[Homonix Rectonia]] is credited with transcribing the code in its classic form. Later, [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] refined it to omit the fourth line, though [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Fae Coven]] restored the Code to its classic form.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />
{{Quote|''There is no emotion, there is peace.''
:''There is no ignorance, there is knowledge.''
:''There is no passion, there is serenity.''
:''There is no chaos, there is harmony.''
:''There is no death, there is the Force.''|[[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr's]] [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]]|<ref name="FF107">{{FactFile|107|JED 7-10|The Jedi Code}}</ref>}}
The Code was not necessarily a strict set of rules, but a general set of guidelines that Jedi were encouraged to keep in mind as they went about the business of the Order. Numerous Jedi teachings interpreted and expounded on the Code in subsequent millennia. These rules, created and embraced by the Jedi Masters, were essential tools in a Jedi's growth. In them, Jedi were encouraged to overcome personal obstacles such as pride and materialism, to understand their small yet important place in the galaxy, and to give every being and point of view equal consideration.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /> 

==Public perception==
For much of Republic history, the Jedi commanded a great deal of respect among the Senate and the populace. Though they often shouldered the blame for ancient struggles and galactic-scale wars with the Sith, centuries of duty to the Republic built them a reputation for fairness and loyalty. As the Republic descended into corruption and division in its last decades, the Jedi struggled to maintain the ideals the Republic's own leadership disregarded or twisted to their own profit.<ref name="Core Rulebook">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> 

[[File:JediMediation-TJP.png|thumb|250px|left|Many in the galaxy respected Jedi wisdom and called on them to mediate disputes.]]
While this high regard made it easy for Jedi to work within the Republic, that popularity created its own problems. During the [[Great Peace of the Republic]], a period marked by relative stability and minimal open conflict, the Jedi were idealized by the public. Legendary tales and holographic entertainments often depicted them as flawless champions—swift, strong, and wise beyond measure. These stories, which frequently began with the greatest heroes of the Order and expanded upon their feats, created nearly impossible standards for Jedi to live up to. As a result, Jedi of this era found themselves burdened by the weight of myth. Disappointed supporters and disillusioned followers became regular hazards for those whose real-world actions could not match the legend.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />  

In the past, when the Jedi began taking active roles in government during the [[New Sith Wars]], their public image began to tarnish. Despite their noble intentions, the public never fully trusted them.<ref name=":0" />   

Following the Ruusan Reformations, the Jedi Order’s policy of recruiting Force-sensitive children at a very young age remained a cornerstone of its continuity. While this practice was sanctioned under the laws of the Galactic Republic, some Masters argued that the presence of the Force within a child could be interpreted as a natural willingness to undertake Jedi training; however, it was not without controversy.<ref name="TJP" />  

For many families, having a child chosen by the Jedi was considered a profound honor, representing both prestige and the opportunity for the child to serve the galaxy. Others, however, found the separation deeply difficult, and some regarded it with resentment. Jedi teachings required initiates to cultivate detachment from personal attachments, including familial bonds. Critics sometimes described the process as coercive, and accusations of kidnapping occasionally circulated, particularly in sensationalized [[HoloNet/Legends|Holonet]] coverage.<ref name="TJP" />  

Within the Order, [[Jedi recruiter|Recruiters]] were acknowledged as performing an essential but often thankless duty, balancing the preservation of Jedi traditions with the emotional complexities of their mission. Nonetheless, limited public outreach and the fact that some Jedi Recruiters, such as [[Morrit Ch'gally/Legends|Moreit Ch'ghally]], recognized they did not always do enough to burnish the Order’s reputation, contributed to negative sentiment and misunderstandings. Jedi were advised not to engage in arguments in such situations, but instead to set examples of selflessness and service.<ref name="TJP" />   

During the era of the Old Republic, Jedi were more numerous and their actions were frequently praised by the public. In the Republic’s final centuries, as the Order’s numbers declined, the supposed shortcomings of the Jedi Order became more apparent. Although Jedi Knights remained highly capable combatants, they were too few to conduct prolonged wars independently on behalf of the Republic. These perceptions were further reinforced by coordinated propaganda and smear campaigns orchestrated by agents of Chancellor Palpatine, contributing to a gradual decline in public confidence in the Jedi Order.<ref>[[Threats of the Galaxy|''Threats of the Galaxy'']]</ref>  

The average citizen never met a Jedi. Many learned of the Jedi through school and history, or inevitably heard of their exploits in the news; however, Jedi numbers were too few compared to the vastness of the Republic and its billions of beings to be particularly visible. Further, the Jedi tended to seclude themselves in their temples and training centers, away from public view. Most citizens simply had no personal connection to, or experience with, a Jedi, and understood the Force even less.<ref name="Core Rulebook" /> 

Individual perceptions of the Jedi Order, ranging from positive to negative, often varied depending on personal experience or the Order's established practices and policies. One negative example was [[Lorn Pavan]], a former clerk at the Jedi Temple, who agreed to let his son, [[Jax Pavan]], be trained as a Jedi. However, due to the Order's strict policy of non-attachment, he was dismissed, which caused him to grow resentful toward the Order and feel that the decision was unjust.<ref name="Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref>

Beyond the borders of the Republic, the Jedi face suspicion and distrust. Some believe their legends to be nothing more than Republic propaganda, while others see them as spies and agents of the Republic itself. In these areas, the Jedi are greeted with hostility as often as with praise.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

The Clone Wars brought the Jedi to the daily public news, as they took command of clone military units and battled the Separatists. Jedi Masters commanded entire armies during the conflict, and the public viewed them as powerful and the wisest of the Order. The worlds they saved regarded them as heroes. The Separatists saw them as one more problem with the Republic. Jedi commanders became a hated enemy of Separatist forces. The public saw Jedi exploits daily—the good and the bad—but the Jedi still stood apart and aloof from most.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

Chancellor Palpatine manipulated Jedi missions during the war, sometimes setting them up for failure or exposing less honorable Jedi actions in the process. As the Jedi changed from peacekeepers to warriors over the years, they lost some of their luster in the public eye. Palpatine's master stroke manipulated the Jedi attempt to arrest and expose him as a Sith Lord into the appearance of an attempted coup, and he used it as the final justification for declaring himself Emperor. Close Jedi allies were shocked by the accusation and watched, unable to stop Palpatine from achieving his long-suspected goals—total power and control over the galaxy.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

The public, however, was more than willing to believe his tales. Scenes of clone troopers willingly firing on their own Jedi commanders convinced many that Palpatine's accusations must be true.<ref name="Core Rulebook" /> 

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], in the Outer Rim Territories, the Jedi were remembered as tragic figures, caught in the same currents of greed and apathy that had come to characterize the final years of the Republic. Among those who recalled the Jedi at the height of their influence, their memory evoked a sense of a bygone era.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /> 

Decades of Imperial rule and relentless propaganda vilified the Jedi Order, branding them as traitors and enemies of peace. For many citizens born after the fall of the Republic, the Jedi were distant myths—figures of suspicion rather than heroes. The Empire worked hard to erase their legacy, purging public records and discouraging even belief in the Force. On some worlds, knowledge of the Jedi and the Force faded almost entirely.

Loyal Imperial citizens were encouraged to denounce suspected Jedi and Force users, contributing to an atmosphere of fear and distrust. Jedi exploits were rewritten or mocked, further turning the public against them.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

Yet not all were convinced. Older individuals who remembered the Clone Wars or the Jedi Order firsthand often noticed clear discrepancies in the Empire’s narrative. In some, this bred doubt toward Imperial rule; in others, it sparked quiet resistance.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

Pockets of belief endured. Dissidents, anti-Imperial activists, and underground movements sought to preserve the truth. Stories of Jedi heroism were whispered in secret, especially among those who suffered under Imperial oppression. Many hoped that some Jedi had survived—and that one day, they would return to challenge the Empire and restore justice.<ref name="Core Rulebook" /> 

===Relations with the Galactic Republic===
Throughout its history, the Jedi Order alternated between maintaining independence from the Republic’s political structures and becoming closely tied to them. Originating as protectors against dangers beyond the galactic frontier, the Jedi dedicated themselves to safeguarding civilization—and for all its flaws, the Republic stood for millennia as its chief representative. From their earliest days, the Jedi resisted assuming authority over others, believing such control could lead toward the dark side. They preferred to act as guardians and observers rather than as rulers, commanders, or power-brokers.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Over the centuries, the Republic occasionally descended into corruption or was steered by leaders who exploited its institutions for personal gain. At other times it faced grave outside threats, most prominently the Sith, whose influence rose and fell across the ages. In such moments, when the stability of civilization seemed at risk, the Jedi were compelled to decide whether direct involvement in the Republic’s affairs was necessary.<ref name="TEGTW" />

At several points in galactic history, the Order chose to intervene. They acted to prevent the destruction of the Tionese, secretly conspired to bring down the Pius Dea regime, and in the turbulent centuries before Ruusan even assumed the office of Supreme Chancellor while administering large portions of Republic space. After each episode, the Jedi relinquished the authority they had taken on, returning to their role as protectors rather than governors. In the later centuries, as the Republic weakened and the Separatist movement grew, the Order again faced debate over whether greater involvement in political and military affairs was necessary.<ref name="TEGTW" /> 

Decades before the Clone Wars, some members of the Order questioned the Jedi’s role in serving the Republic. Among them was the prominent Jedi Count Dooku, who questioned whether the Jedi Order had evolved into little more than a glorified security service aligned with the interests of the Galactic Senate.<ref name="UVG">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref>

Throughout history, there were moments when tension arose between the Jedi and the Republic, as an example after the end of the Great War. Devastated by the return of the Sith Empire, the Republic criticized the Jedi for failing to defend them.<ref name="TOR Encyclopedia" />

===Jedi Order relations with other Force traditions===
In addition to the Jedi and Sith, numerous species and cultures across the galaxy developed their own unique Force traditions. These traditions were often deeply rooted in local customs, philosophies, or spiritual beliefs, and operated independently of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

The Jedi generally pursued diplomatic relations with such groups and occasionally sought to bring them into alignment with Jedi teachings. However, many preferred to remain autonomous. As long as these traditions did not engage in dark side practices or threaten galactic stability, the Jedi typically adopted a policy of cautious non-interference, allowing them to follow their own path.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

Most of these groups had relatively few Force-sensitive individuals, and even fewer who could rival a fully trained Jedi Knight or Master. Nonetheless, the Jedi maintained occasional contact and monitored them—sometimes through conventional means, other times through farseeing—stepping in if signs of danger emerged.<ref name="Core Rulebook" />

Examples include dark side groups such as the [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]], whom the Order observed closely. In more serious cases, the Jedi were prepared to take direct action, as they did against the [[Ember of Vahl]], a cult they deemed dangerous due to its dark and destructive tendencies—and which the Jedi ultimately decimated.<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Locations==
{{Quote|Don't the Jedi have this reputation for, well, austerity?''"<br />"''They like you to think that, yes! But have big honking Temple on Coruscant! Not come cheap!|[[Gar Gastinin]] and [[Vilmarh Grahrk]]|<ref name="Star Wars (1998) 40">[[Star Wars (1998) 40|''Star Wars'' (1998) 40]]</ref>}}
From a historical context, the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] was the Order's last great headquarters, serving as its governmental center and home to the largest active [[Jedi academy]] in the galaxy and the great [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]]. In addition to the Coruscant Temple, the Order had been headquartered on Ossus for the greatest number of years before the planet's devastation during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], and only briefly on the Order's homeworld Tython, both at the Order's conception and during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]. In addition to the main academy the Jedi Order had outposts on many worlds and operated mobile academies throughout its history.

===Coruscant===
{{Quote|This was our tower of guard: our fortress watch upon the dark. This was the Jedi Temple.|[[Vergere]] to [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]]|<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Traitor">''[[The New Jedi Order: Traitor]]''</ref>}}
The [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] was the main Jedi headquarters from the end of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] in [[3996 BBY]] until the beginning of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. Despite its impressive appearance, the Jedi Temple was a relatively modern building in comparison to some of Coruscant's others&mdash;the temple was built on a plot of land which had been awarded to the Jedi Order by the Senate after [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] attempted [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Hyperspace War)|invasion]] of the capital in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]. The Senate hoped that having such a large Jedi presence on the capital would leave the planet less susceptible to invasions. From this site, the four [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councils]] took care of the administrative, strategic, and spiritual needs of the Jedi Order, ensuring that it met the needs of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and its vast multitudes of citizens.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

[[File:Jedi_temple2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].]]

When the land was awarded to the Order by the Senate, the Jedi were at first reluctant to build a citadel there&mdash;they held the belief that the Order was not a military organization, and that a military-oriented building would be a contradiction to their code. Instead of taking the Senate's proposition, the Council authorized the construction of a meditative and training center instead, some of which helped preserve the rapidly diminishing nature of Coruscant. Eventually, the original meditative and training center grew vastly in size and complexity, until it began to resemble the sprawling world on which it was located.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /> New chambers within the Jedi Temple included the [[Room of a Thousand Fountains/Legends|Room of a Thousand Fountains]], which contained a huge greenhouse, flowing waters and cascades. Also included in the expansive temple were [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] training areas as well as areas which provided views of vast holographic star maps.<ref name="Jedi Temple in the Databank">{{DB|location|jeditemple|Jedi Temple}}</ref>

The Jedi Temple had five spires; one for each of its four Councils, and a larger spire which contained the sacred manuscripts of the founding Jedi.<ref name="Jedi Temple in the Databank" /> The Jedi High Council chambers were located in the southwest tower, while the [[Council of Reconciliation/Legends|Council of Reconciliation]] chambers were located in the southeast tower. The northeast and northwest towers were occupied by the [[Council of Reassignment/Legends|Council of Reassignment]] and the [[Council of First Knowledge/Legends|Council of First Knowledge]].<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /> While the Temple was sacked many times throughout the Order long history, the facility was last abandoned by the Old Jedi Order following [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]]. As part of the execution of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] led the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] into the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], intent on destroying the Jedi. Although the Jedi Temple was not destroyed, it was badly damaged, with smoke billowing out for all to see.<ref name="ROTS" /> The structure proved to be the most virulent of all Jedi temples, as it would continue to be the Order's home following [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] rebuilding of the [[New Jedi Order|Order]]. The [[New Jedi Temple|rebuilt]] Temple would serve as home to the Order on an off for several generations until finally being occupied by the [[One Sith]] at the end of the [[Sith–Imperial War]].

===Ossus===
[[File:GreatJediLibrary.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Great Jedi Library on Ossus]]
The great [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] was the home of the Jedi for the longest, continuous time span; beginning with the Jedi migration from Tython circa [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]]<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> until the world's ruination during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. The crown jewel of the Jedi-controlled planet was the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]], an immense library for Jedi students constructed under the direction of [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]. The library was a repository for knowledge of all kinds, while the world served as a training center for many Jedi students. The vast amounts of information the library contained were sorted in various different ways, depending on age and importance. Most of the data was contained on reader tapes and holographic media, although some of the more ancient knowledge was stored on traditional paper scrolls and books. Although the ancient books and scrolls were eventually translated onto electronic forms, the [[Chamber of Antiquities/Legends|Chamber of Antiquities]] preserved the ancient writing for historical purposes.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

The library also held knowledge forbidden to the Jedi, such as ancient [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]], which Odan-Urr had decided to keep. The [[Draethos/Legends|Draethos]] Jedi Master's reasoning was that all knowledge&mdash;even knowledge of evil&mdash;would be useful in the defense of justice. Only those who had been approved by the Jedi Council, as well as Odan-Urr (as the [[Keeper of Antiquities]]), were allowed access to these [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]], and even then they were only permitted to do so under strict supervision. During the height of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] in [[3996 BBY]], fallen Jedi [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] visited Ossus to recruit new members to his cause. While there, he entered the Chamber of Antiquities, slaying Odan-Urr to get to one of the Sith holocrons. Afterwards, Ossus became a battlefield for the Jedi/Republic army, which eventually defeated the Sith Empire. Meanwhile, a supernova was threatening to devastate the planet. After Ossus had been evacuated, Exar Kun and his apprentice, [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], arrived at the Great Jedi Library, looking to plunder the remaining artifacts before the supernova's shockwave destroyed them. However, [[Neti/Legends|Neti]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ood Bnar]] managed to foil the two [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|darksiders]], metamorphosing into a powerful tree; he sacrificed his life to protect a vault of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] from Kun and his apprentice.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" />

===Dantooine===
The [[Jedi Enclave]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] was a secret Jedi training center located on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] prior to the [[Jedi Civil War]]. The Enclave consisted of several levels, the first of which included a council chamber, sparring rooms, and dormitories,<ref name="KOTOR" /> while the sublevel consisted of common rooms, classrooms, and a medical bay, as well as an archive room only accessible by Jedi Masters.<ref name="KOTORII" /> The Enclave was built upon a courtyard, which led out into Dantooine's [[Khoonda plains|plains]]. At the center of the building was a circular open-air room, with several trees at the center of a walkway.<ref name="KOTOR" />

[[File:Originalenclave.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Jedi Enclave during the Jedi Civil War.]]
The [[Dantooine Jedi Enclave Council]] held its meetings in a small council chamber, similar to the one on Coruscant and had jurisdiction over the Jedi in the part of the Outer Rim that included Dantooine and Taris.<ref name="DarkHorse">{{DHBoards|subdomain=www|url=boards/viewtopic.php?p=128708#128708|thread=KNIGHTS of the OLD REPUBLIC #5 -- All this over a dream!?|user=[[John Jackson Miller]]|date=2006-06-03|time=09:27|quote=The satellite council on Dantooine has a degree of local jurisdiction over affairs in the part of the Outer Rim where Taris can be found. This is their backyard, so to speak. Further, it's been established that the Padawans started on Dantooine before being assigned to the Taris satellite academy -- another reason for a particular interest in events.}}</ref> Around the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Council was responsible for healing Darth Revan's destroyed mind and inserting a new identity into his brain, and after the [[destruction of Taris]], retraining him in the ways of the Jedi. The Council was dissolved after Darth Malak's bombardment of the Jedi Enclave during the Jedi Civil War, which left the Enclave as ruins which would be abandoned and reoccupied over the next few centuries.<ref name="KOTORII" />

===Tython===
The birthplace of the Jedi Order, Tython was devastated at the close of the [[Force Wars]] and swiftly abandoned by a Jedi Order which wanted nothing to do with a growing Galactic Republic. Tython would not be revisited for many long millennium as the Order grew on Ossus and later Coruscant. Forgotten by many, it wasn't until the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] that Jedi [[Satele Shan]] repaved the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to the lost world and established a new [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Temple]] there. As the Jedi Order relocated form Coruscant to their lush new home, Tython's mysteries were explored in depth by eager young [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] and curious [[Jedi archaeologist]]s. Despite an enormous recolonization effort by the Jedi during the Cold War, Tython was eventually abandoned once more and left an ash-covered waste.<ref name="SWTOR" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Jedi Order originated in the rough draft as the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor's]] bodyguard.<ref name="Databank" /> They became affiliated with the ''[[Republica Galactica]]'' in the second draft.<ref name="Empire DB">{{DB|organization|theempire|Empire, the}}</ref> Later, when composing background information for licensees in [[1977]], [[George Lucas]] described the Jedi Order as being "several hundred thousand" strong before the Purge.<ref name="Making of">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

For the word "Jedi," Lucas took inspiration from the [[Wikipedia:Japanese language|Japanese]] term "[[Wikipedia:Jidaigeki|Jidaigeki]]," which refers to a drama set set during the [[Wikipedia:Edo period|Edo period]] of Japanese history, when [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]] were still in activity.<ref name="Episode I Scrapbook" />
